title: How Sweden found Chernobyl before Moscow said a word ☢️
subject: chernobyl
description:
Would a nuclear accident stay secret that long today? 👇

On 28 April 1986, radiation monitors at Sweden's Forsmark nuclear plant were set off by workers' shoes. The plant was fine. The fallout had come from Chernobyl in the Soviet Union, which denied any accident until that evening.

Sources: Kyiv Post, "When Sweden Got Wind of an Apocalypse: the Man Who Raised the Chornobyl Alarm" (2026); European Parliament, via Watching the Swedes, "How Sweden exposed the Chernobyl catastrophe" (2019); Wikipedia: Chernobyl disaster, Forsmark Nuclear Power Plant
tags: how the world found out about chernobyl

scenes.text: A worker's shoes set off Sweden's nuclear alarms.
Just before 7 a.m. on 28 April 1986, at Forsmark, north of Stockholm. Every worker who walked through after him set it off too.
The plant was fine. Meteorologist Christer Persson traced the air back to the southwestern Soviet Union.
That evening, it admitted a reactor at Chernobyl, about 1,100 kilometers away, had exploded two days earlier.
Sweden found the disaster from radioactive dust on a pair of shoes.
